name: hcapp_getHashTrash
description: Returns the HashTrash article for a run. Published articles (HashTrashStatus = 1) are returned to any authenticated user. Draft articles (HashTrashStatus = 0) are returned only when HC6.CheckKennelPermission 'viewHashTrashDrafts' allows the caller for @kennelId (feature 'View Hash Trash drafts': those who can save can see drafts; SuperAdmin always) — otherwise content and status come back NULL with no error. If the event does not exist in that kennel (or is deleted) the rowset is EMPTY (zero rows); if the article has not been written, one row of NULLs. Callers treat NULL content as 'no article'. Auth: HC6.ValidateAppAuth (spNumber 54, @param NULL). Read SP — no success envelope on the happy path. New feature — no HC5 equivalent.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Registered device UUID. Passed to HC6.ValidateAppAuth for auth resolution.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived auth token validated against DeviceSecret.

parameters.name: kennelId
parameters.description: Kennel that owns the event. Required — null or zero-UUID triggers validation error. Defaults to NULL when omitted (2026-10-13).

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: Event to fetch HashTrash for. Required — null or zero-UUID triggers validation error. Defaults to NULL when omitted (2026-10-13).

rowsets.name: ErrorEnvelope
rowsets.description: Compact error envelope on auth failure (ValidateAppAuth) or missing ids (1234/2): { success=0, errorCode, errorType }, followed by StandardErrorResult at index 1. Mutually exclusive with the HashTrash rowset. Runtime errors are logged to HC.ErrorLog and re-thrown (THROW).

rowsets.name: HashTrash
rowsets.description: Zero rows when no event matches (@eventId + @kennelId, deleted = 0); otherwise exactly one row. All three columns NULL when the article has not been written (HashTrashStatus IS NULL); content and status NULL (headline still returned) when the article is a draft and the caller lacks viewHashTrashDrafts. Mutually exclusive with ErrorEnvelope.

columns.name: headline
columns.description: HC.Event.HashTrashHeadline (NVARCHAR(500) NULL). Returned whatever the status — a draft's headline is visible to everyone; only content and status are withheld.

columns.name: content
columns.description: HC.Event.HashTrashContent — the markdown body. NULL when: no article exists, HashTrashStatus IS NULL, status=0 (draft) and caller lacks mismanagement access, or event not found.

columns.name: status
columns.description: HC.Event.HashTrashStatus — 0 = draft, 1 = published. NULL when content is NULL (same conditions). Never returns the raw status for a draft the caller cannot see.

rowsets.description: Returned at index 1 alongside the ErrorEnvelope (index 0) on auth or validation errors.

sideEffects: INSERT HC.ErrorLog on missing ids (line 74) and from the CATCH block (lines 112-114, after ROLLBACK)

codeSmells.detail: These parameters have no SQL default, so a call that omits one is refused by SQL Server before the procedure runs (unlogged empty 500): @deviceId, @accessToken. On 2026-10-13 every parameter whose body already handled NULL (and every sync watermark) was given a default; these remain because they are the auth pair or the body never checks them for NULL.

codeSmells.issue: Zero rows returned when event not found (vs one row of NULLs)
codeSmells.detail: Lines 104-107 filter HC.Event by id, kennel and deleted = 0, so a wrong kennelId or a deleted event yields ZERO rows while 'no article yet' yields ONE row of NULLs. Callers must handle both; the app's firstRow() helper returns null for either, so in practice both read as 'no article'.
The SP sets SET NOCOUNT ON but not SET XACT_ABORT ON. Since this is a read-only SP this is harmless but inconsistent with the HC6 SP standard.

codeSmells.issue: A draft's headline is not withheld
codeSmells.detail: Line 91 returns HashTrashHeadline unconditionally while lines 92-103 withhold content and status for a draft the caller may not see. A non-admin can read the headline of an unpublished article.
